rows.stableSchemaDescription:
Treat the crates of a Cargo workspace as Turborepo packages.

When enabled, Rust crates are discovered via `cargo metadata` and participate in the package graph: they resolve in `--filter` expressions, propagate `--affected`, and appear in `turbo query`. Filtered builds execute each selected crate. Unfiltered builds prefer entrypoints, falling back to libraries when no entrypoints exist. Entrypoints also expose `run` and `dev`. The `test`, `check`, `lint`, and `format` tasks are selectable per crate with `--filter`. An unfiltered run executes one workspace-wide Cargo verification command; filtered runs use the selected crates, or the workspace command when the workspace package is selected directly.

All crates implicitly register `build` and the verification tasks; entrypoints with one binary also register `run` and `dev`. The workspace package registers the verification tasks. Normal task definitions configure or override these defaults, and package configuration can exclude them with `extends: false`.

Task caching uses Cargo-derived inputs and caches entrypoint build deliverables. Library builds and formatting default to uncached. This feature is experimental.
prerequisites: Change only one experimental flag at a time

rows.expectedBenefit: Must be measured for the specific named consumer; no generic percentage claimed.
rows.correctnessCase: Run the feature-specific positive/negative matrix on both pinned native clients; do not inherit another flag's result.
rows.disposition: Retain absent root Cargo discovery; preserve the two standalone Tauri crates and explicit sidecar/native CI ownership.

rows.stableSchemaDescription: Use task-level `inputs` globs to determine which tasks to re-run when files change in `turbo watch`. When enabled, only tasks whose declared inputs match the changed files are re-executed, rather than re-running all tasks in changed packages.
prerequisites: Change only one experimental flag at a time

rows.canarySchemaDescription: Include file executable permissions in task hashes. Disabled by default. Enabling this flag changes all task hashes. On Unix, any executable bit marks a regular file as executable. On Windows, files are non-executable. Symlink permissions and other permission bits do not affect hashes.
prerequisites: Stable support or a separately approved canary-only profile.
Native executable-bit input perturbation and symlink/non-executable permission controls on supported platforms.
Requalify hashes and epochs before activation; this flag changes all task hashes.
rows.beepUseCase: Assess executable-bit changes as semantic task inputs across Linux, worktrees and hosted runners.
rows.expectedBenefit: Correct invalidation for permission-sensitive work; no timing or hit-rate benefit is claimed.
rows.correctnessCase: Compare unchanged bytes with executable-bit changes and other mode-bit controls; preserve Unix/Windows and symlink distinctions.
rows.disposition: Remain disabled; qualify the canary-only behavior before proposing a profile-specific activation.
